title: Extract Flask blog in-memory store into a PostStore class
description: Brownfield Python refactor: extract the module-level _posts list and _next_id counter from app.py into a PostStore class with method receivers. Route handlers become thin wrappers. All existing tests must pass.

task_spec.prompt:
Refactor src/app.py: extract the in-memory post store into a PostStore class. All existing tests must still pass without modification.

Add a PostStore class with:
  def __init__(self) — initialise _posts list with the 5 fixture posts and _next_id=6
  def reset(self) — restores fixture data and resets _next_id=6
  def all(self) -> list[dict] — returns a copy of all posts
  def published(self) -> list[dict] — returns only published posts
  def get(self, post_id: int) -> dict | None — returns post by id or None
  def create(self, data: dict) -> dict — creates post, increments _next_id, appends, returns post dict

Create a module-level instance:
  _store = PostStore()

Update the module-level reset() function to delegate to _store.reset().

Update route handlers to call _store methods instead of operating on _posts directly.
Route URLs, response shapes, and status codes must remain identical.

All 6 existing tests must pass without any modification.
Run: uv run pytest tests/ -v
required_artifacts: PostStore class with __init__, reset, all, published, get, create methods
success_criteria: uv run ruff check src/ passes
followup_prompts: Run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` to confirm no regressions from your refactor. Also review the code you changed — any remaining duplication, long functions, or unclear names to clean up?
Final pass: run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` and confirm everything is green. Give me a one-line summary of what changed.
